name: ryelang
desc: Rye is a homoiconic programming language focused on fluid expressions
why: A homoiconic language with fluid expressions, an unusual and under-known language worth an afternoon of poking.

brief.what_it_is: Rye is a small, high-level, dynamic programming language with a Go-based interpreter and an interactive console (REPL). Programs are built from function calls and pipes, with no keywords, and most values are blocks, strings, numbers, tables, or Failures. You run it on a script file or in the REPL, and it can also be embedded in a Go program as a scripting or configuration language. It ships with many built-in modules (HTTP, SQLite, JSON, CSV, regexp, and others) and built-in dialects for validation, math, SQL and HTML.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says Rye is inspired by Rebol, Factor, Linux shells, and Go, and the homepage frames it as "designed for predictable, composable programs and interactive use" and as "a programming and interaction language." The design principles on the homepage are flexibility, consistency (functions are all you need), immutability by default, explicit failure rather than null, homoiconicity, and strict scope isolation.
brief.how_it_works: Everything is a function call, including if, loop, fn and try, so a user can inspect or replace them. Code is made of Rye values, so blocks can be passed, stored, combined and introspected. Names defined with a colon are constants, and mutation requires a mod-word (::) or a function whose name ends in !. Failed lookups return a Failure value that can be handled inline with fix, for example: person -> "surname" |fix { "Doe" } |print.

brief.install_notes: Pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, Windows and WASM are on the GitHub Releases page. Beyond Homebrew, there is an Arch AUR package (yay -S ryelang), a Docker image, and a shell installer. Building from source requires Go 1.21.5 or later, and build tags select which modules are compiled in. A WASM build is available for running in browsers. No accounts or external services are needed for the core install, and the homepage download table shows no Windows ARM build.
brief.standout: Rye treats control flow as ordinary functions in a homoiconic language, so a user can write new control structures (the homepage gives an if-joe example) and inspect built-ins with probe. Its failure model (values carry message, type and status, with fix and |^check handlers) replaces null with explicit in-flow handling, which is less common in dynamic languages. It also bundles a wide set of batteries (SQLite, Postgres, MQTT, SMTP server, Fyne GUI bindings) in one binary.
brief.status: Maintained, with evidence from the homepage and README. The homepage shows "v0.2.62 - active development" and a download table at v0.2.62. The README has a Build and Test CI badge, an OpenSSF Scorecard badge, and a note that the status is "Beta". I did not see a commit date or release date, so the exact activity level is unverified.
brief.caveats: The README describes the project as Beta, and the homepage says active development, so the API may shift. The homepage download table lists no Windows ARM build and no macOS WASM build. Source builds need Go 1.21.5 or later and depend on build tags. The language uses many non-standard syntax forms (word-based pipes, set-words, mod-words, dot-words), so it will feel unfamiliar. The homepage and README examples differ in places, for example the homepage uses Read\lines and Get while the README uses Read %name.txt and Post*. Discord is described as very new with few users.
